## What it is

- Mesa/Boogie began with Randall Smith modifying Fender amps; in the 1970s he **cascaded** gain stages for far more distortion (Wikipedia, "Mesa Boogie").
- The **Dual Rectifier** came in **1991**, inspired by the Soldano SLO-100, with a "raw, aggressive bass-heavy sound" and a diamond-plate face (Wikipedia).
- Users named by Wikipedia: Korn, Tool, Soundgarden, Foo Fighters, Blink-182.

## How it makes its sound

- **Cascaded gain stages**: valve after valve, each clipping what the last one clipped. That is where the high gain comes from (the number of stages here is the site's choice).
- A **Master** volume after the tone stack sets how loud, and how hard the power valves work, separately from the preamp's Gain.
- The name is the rectifier: a switch picks **silicon diodes** (tight) or a **valve** rectifier (more sag, "spongy"). The switch and the Mode names (Raw / Vintage / Modern) are from general knowledge here: unverified.
- The **tone stack** (Treble, Middle, Bass) is a passive network of three capacitors and resistors: it can only cut. This page computes its curve exactly from the component values, with the formula Yeh and Smith published in 2006 (checked there against a circuit simulator); the graph under the panel shows it. The values used here are the site's guess.

## The amp

The Mesa/Boogie Dual Rectifier's control panel, drawn after photos (positions approximate, no logos). Drag a knob (or use the arrow keys), click a switch, then press a ▶ button. The guitar is this site's pickup model; **Pedals in front** puts one of the site's pedal models before the amp. Nobody has compared the sound with a real amp. The graph shows the tone controls and the cabinet (the valves' distortion is left out of it).

## Guided tour

```{=html}
<div class="amp-step" data-amp="rect" data-set="{&quot;gain&quot;:2,&quot;master&quot;:5,&quot;mode&quot;:&quot;raw&quot;}" data-play="chord"><p><b>Gain 2, Raw.</b> Crunch.</p></div>
<div class="amp-step" data-amp="rect" data-set="{&quot;gain&quot;:6,&quot;master&quot;:5,&quot;mode&quot;:&quot;modern&quot;}" data-play="riff"><p><b>Gain 6, Modern.</b> Full high gain.</p></div>
<div class="amp-step" data-amp="rect" data-set="{&quot;gain&quot;:6,&quot;master&quot;:5,&quot;mode&quot;:&quot;modern&quot;,&quot;middle&quot;:1,&quot;bass&quot;:8}" data-play="riff"><p><b>Mid 1, Bass 8.</b> The scooped metal sound.</p></div>
<div class="amp-step" data-amp="rect" data-set="{&quot;gain&quot;:4,&quot;master&quot;:8,&quot;mode&quot;:&quot;vintage&quot;,&quot;rect&quot;:&quot;tube&quot;}" data-play="chord"><p><b>Tube rectifier, Master 8.</b> Looser, more sag.</p></div>
<div class="amp-step" data-amp="rect" data-set="{&quot;gain&quot;:7,&quot;master&quot;:4,&quot;mode&quot;:&quot;modern&quot;}" data-play="lead"><p><b>A lead line.</b> Long sustain.</p></div>
```
